correctness.rationale: Each center has two singleton goods, so every external one-good-removal leaves a singleton valued 0 or 1 under either potential comparison. A center holding no liked good but liking any external good necessarily fails EFX, so satisfied active centers yield distinct center-good representatives and cannot exceed a maximum matching. Matching goods placed with interested affiliated agents make all matched centers have realized value at least 1, meeting every possible postdeletion comparison under all four own-value conventions. Inactive centers never fail; the Hall-deficiency formula follows. Inter-EF1 is automatic for singleton child bundles. Direct exhaustive and sampled original-definition checks in VERIFY.cpp succeed; six-good capacity-three boundary follows from an elementary two-case split.

value.rationale: When strong two-level EFX is infeasible, the minimal number of noncompliant centers is a concrete welfare-administration invariant. An exact all-size deficiency formula, a polynomial constructive optimum shared across four semantics, and the sharp three-person failure boundary give substantially more information than a yes/no counterexample, while avoiding an arbitrary finite census. The simplicity of Hall's theorem is acknowledged; the value lies in the exact hierarchical EFX reduction.
